manual.title: User manual
manual.intro: modelkeeper catalogs your 3D printing models on your PC and NAS, so you can find them, tag them and keep track of them. The app only reads your model files: it never moves, changes or deletes a file – not even duplicates.

sections.title: Getting started
body: 1. Click **Folders** at the bottom left, then **Add folder…**. Choose your model folder on the NAS (preferably by its network path such as \\fritz.nas\…, not by a drive letter) and, if you like, more folders on the PC.
2. Click **Scan**. modelkeeper lists all model files, computes a fingerprint (hash) of each – including files inside zip, rar and 7z archives – and detects the models from them.
3. When the scan is done, click **All models** on the left. Everything that was found is there.

The first scan of a large collection on the NAS takes long, often a day or more. The estimated time left is shown below the progress bar. You can use the app meanwhile, stop the scan with **Pause**, or simply close the app: everything hashed so far is kept, even in the middle of a large file. After closing, the scan continues by itself at the next start; after **Pause**, only when you click **Resume**. After that, only new and changed files are read.
The first folder level below a root folder counts as the creator (e.g. "Atlas Miniatures"). If your folder is organized differently, turn off **First folder level is the creator** for it.

Keep the modelkeeper folder itself (with modelkeeper.exe and data) on the PC, not on the NAS: on a network share the catalog can be damaged. If it is there anyway, the app does not start and tells you what to do.

sections.title: Finding models
body: On the left are the views of your collection: **All models**, **To catalog** (models without tags), **Favorites** and **Recently added**. Below are your **Creators**, the most used **Tags** and the **Locations**. One click filters the list, a second click removes the filter. Filters combine, e.g. "To catalog" by one creator.
The search field searches names, creators, tags, notes and paths. Results appear while you type; word beginnings are enough ("orc war" finds "Orc Warlord").

- **Filters** opens more criteria: tag, creator, folder, file type, supports and print status, and checkboxes such as **Duplicates**, **Single location only**, **Offline** or **Broken archives**. Active filters are shown as chips below the search field; ✕ removes one.
- **Sort**: by name (by relevance while searching) or **Recently added**.
- At the top right you switch between **Grid** and **List** and choose the **tile size**.

- The **arrow keys** move through the tiles, **Home**/**End** jump to the start and the end, **F** makes the selected model a favorite, **Esc** closes the detail view. In the search field, **arrow down** moves into the list.
Marks on the tiles: **new** means the model has no tags yet. **!** means files disappeared since the last scan. The list view also shows at how many places a model is.

sections.title: Cataloging
body: **To catalog** lists every model without tags – work through your collection bit by bit:
1. Click the first model. The detail view opens on the right, with the cursor already in the tag field.
2. Type tags, several separated by commas, and press **Enter**. Accept dashed suggestions from the folder names with +, all at once with **Accept all**.
3. As soon as the model has tags, it leaves the list and the next one is selected. **←**/**→** or **Skip** move on without tagging.

Pictures in the model folder appear as a gallery below the large picture in the detail view; a click enlarges them, **←**/**→** browse, **Esc** closes. **Use as thumbnail** makes the picture shown the tile's picture.

sections.title: Editing a model
body: Click a model to open the detail view on the right.
- **Name**: use the pencil next to the name. A name you set is kept on every scan.
- **Print status**: not printed, printed successfully, or failed.
- **Supports**: detected from folder and file names (supported, presupported, unsupported). You can set it yourself; **Automatic** leaves it to the detection again.
- **Tags**: type and click **Add**. Dashed tags are suggestions from the folder names – accept with + or dismiss with ✕. Suggestions are never applied on their own.
- **Notes**: saved as soon as you leave the field.
- **Found in** lists all places of the model, **Files** all its files with variant and identical copies. **Show in Explorer** opens the folder (for files inside archives, the archive).

modelkeeper makes thumbnails itself: from an image in the model folder, the preview inside a 3MF file, or rendered from the STL. **Change thumbnail** lets you pick another image of the model, an image of your own (**Choose image…**), or go back with **Back to automatic**.
**3D preview** shows the model in 3D: drag to rotate, right mouse button to pan, mouse wheel to zoom. **Use view as thumbnail** saves the current view as the thumbnail.

**Open in slicer** opens the likely file (a slicer project first, otherwise the main file); ▾ lets you choose another one. The slicer always gets a read-only copy, never the original – it cannot overwrite anything in your collection. Which program is used is set under Settings → **Slicer**. Save slicer projects somewhere of your own; the copies are removed after 7 days.

sections.title: Several models at once
body: **Ctrl**+click adds single models to the selection, **Shift**+click a whole range. A bar for all selected models then appears at the top:
- add or remove tags,
- add to or remove from the favorites,
- **Merge** into one of the models – when the detection wrongly split one model into several. Tags and notes are kept.
**Clear selection** ends the multiple selection.

sections.title: Correcting the detection
body: modelkeeper suggests what a model is; you decide. Folders with typical part names (Supported, Parts, Base, STL …) and size variants (S_, M_, 32mm, 75mm …) are added to the model above them. An archive starts out as a model of its own.
Under **Correct** in the detail view:
- **Folder above is the model**: everything in the folder above becomes one model.
- **Not a model of its own**: the folder belongs to the model above.
- **Split into subfolders**: every subfolder becomes a model of its own.
- **Split off this location**: one place of a model with several places becomes a model of its own.
- **Undo corrections**: the detection decides on its own again.
Corrections are kept on every new scan. You can extend the lists **Part folders** and **Size variants** under Settings → **Model detection**.

sections.title: Folders and scans
body: - **Live**: local folders are watched; changes are picked up automatically after a short pause.
- **NAS folders** are not watched live but rescanned on a schedule (set under **Settings**). If the NAS is unreachable, all entries stay and are shown as **Offline**.
- **Scan** reads only new and changed files.
- **Full check** reads every file again. It finds damaged or silently changed files and can take long, especially over the NAS.
- **Detect models** applies the detection again without reading files.

- **Pause** stops a running scan. The folder is then not scanned automatically (not live, not on schedule, not at start) until you click **Resume**, even after a restart. The running scan is also shown, with pause, at the bottom of the sidebar.
Each folder shows numbers on files, size, duplicates, archives and problems. **Problems in the last scan** lists, for example, damaged or password-protected archives.
**Share hashes**: if someone else scans the same folder (e.g. the same NAS), they can **import** your hashes instead of reading everything themselves. Tags, notes and favorites are not included.

sections.title: Deactivating and deleting folders
body: **Deactivate…** takes a folder out of scanning and watching. Everything you entered – tags, notes, favorites, print status, corrections – is kept. Models that only exist there stay visible and are marked. If you add the same folder again later, it is reactivated and everything is linked up again.
Deactivated folders are listed at the bottom of the **Folders** page. There you also find **Delete permanently from the catalog**:
- The dialog shows how many models with your data will have no location left. If the number is above 0, you have to type it. **Look at these models** shows them first.
- A backup is made automatically right before deleting. If it fails, nothing is deleted.
- If the files of such a model show up in a folder again later, it is linked up again automatically.
In both cases, the files on disk are not touched.

sections.title: Backups and restoring
body: modelkeeper backs up the catalog, the settings and the thumbnails you chose into the folder data\backups inside the modelkeeper folder automatically:
- once a day, if something changed since the last backup – at start and also when the app stays open for days,
- before every update of the catalog to a new version,
- before a folder is deleted permanently and before file types are changed,
- any time with **Create backup now** (Settings → **Data & backups**).
It keeps the 14 newest daily backups and all others of the last 90 days, and always at least the 3 newest. Every backup is checked after it is written.

**Backup outside this PC**: under Settings, choose a second backup folder, e.g. an external drive, your Dropbox folder or a separate share on the NAS (not the model folder). Every backup is copied there, together with modelkeeper.exe and instructions (README.txt).

**Restore test**: once a day and after every new backup, modelkeeper checks that the newest backup can really be restored – preferably the copy in the second folder. The result is shown in the settings; if the test fails, the sidebar shows a warning sign at **Settings**. **Test now** checks right away.

**Restoring**: under **Show and restore backups**, choose a backup and click **Restore…**. At the next start, modelkeeper replaces catalog, settings and thumbnails with the backup's state. The current state is saved as a backup first – so you can undo a restore the same way.

**New PC**: copy modelkeeper.exe from the second backup folder into a new folder, create data\backups in it, copy the backup folder you want into it and start modelkeeper. The app offers the backup for restoring.
If the catalog is damaged at start, modelkeeper stops before anything is written and shows the backups to restore from.

sections.title: Undo, export and moving folders
body: **Undo**: every change of tags, fields and favorites can be undone – click **Undo** in the message at the bottom, or press **Ctrl+Z** anywhere outside a text field. Settings → **Recent changes** lists the last changes. A model that was changed in another way since (e.g. merged) is left as it is.
Corrections of the detection – merge, split, "is a model", "not a model", detach, reset – can be undone the same way: the folders are detected again and every model gets its ID, tags and notes back.
Notes are saved while you type; "Saved" below the field confirms it.

**Export**: Settings → **Export and import** → **Export…** writes one JSON file with everything you entered: tags, notes, favorites, print status, edited names and creators, origin and license, corrections, the thumbnails you chose, your folders and detection settings. Every backup contains the same file as catalog-export.json – also every copy in the second backup folder.

**Import**: **Import…** reads such a file. modelkeeper shows first what it contains and how its models are found here: by their ID, at the same place, or by their files (fingerprints) even if they were moved or renamed. Models not found yet keep their data and are linked up as soon as a scan finds their files. The import only adds – nothing you entered is removed – and a backup is made first.
**For someone else**: export on your PC, give the file to the other person; they import it, choose where the folders are on their PC (or add them), and scan.

**Folder moved** (new NAS, other drive letter): Folders → **Change path…** at the folder. modelkeeper checks a sample of the files at the new place, makes a backup, changes the path and scans. The folder keeps all tags, notes and corrections. Do not add the new place as a second folder – the tags would stay with the old one.

**Waiting for files**: models from an import whose files were not found yet are listed under this view on the left (only while there are any). Remove a model there if its files are gone for good. Import and **Change path…** also work while a scan runs: the scan is paused for it and continues afterwards. Corrections of the detection made during a scan are saved right away and applied when the scan is done.
**Tags**: Settings → **Tags** renames or deletes a tag for all its models at once; renaming to an existing tag merges both (typos). Undoable.

sections.title: Installing and moving
body: modelkeeper is portable: modelkeeper.exe and its data folder (next to it, called data) belong together. Put the folder somewhere permanent, e.g. C:\Users\<you>\modelkeeper – not in Downloads, not in a OneDrive or Dropbox folder (modelkeeper warns), and not inside the zip file (modelkeeper refuses to start there, the catalog would be lost).

To move it to another folder, disk or PC: close modelkeeper and move or copy the whole folder. Everything goes along. At the next start modelkeeper notices the move; if model folders moved along (a portable disk with another drive letter, model folders next to the app), it offers to update their paths.
If the model files move on their own (new NAS), use Folders → **Change path…**.
Settings → **Configuration** exports the settings and the folder list as JSON, to set up another PC the same way; **Export and import** carries the cataloging work.

sections.title: Settings
body: - **Language**: German, English, or the system language.
- **Rescan NAS folders automatically**: how often NAS folders are checked. A manual scan resets the timer.
- **Data & backups**: where the data is, create and restore backups.
- **Slicer**: which program **Open in slicer** uses. Without a choice, Windows uses the program that belongs to the file type.
- **Backup outside this PC**: second backup folder and restore test.
- **File types**: which files are cataloged. Removing a type drops its entries from the catalog – the files themselves are not touched; a backup is made first.
- **Model detection**: **Part folders** are added to the model above, **Size variants** (e.g. S_Orc, Orc_XL) are recognized as variants. Your corrections are kept.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
body: **Does modelkeeper change my files?** No. The app only reads model files. It writes only into its own data folder next to modelkeeper.exe.
**Can the slicer change my files?** No. **Open in slicer** always passes a read-only copy from data\open, never the file in your collection.
**Is hashing risky for my files?** No. Hashing only reads files. Pausing, closing the app or a crash cannot damage a file; the scan continues where it stopped.
**I moved a folder – are my tags gone?** No. Moved files are recognized by their hash; tags, notes and status stay with the model once the new place has been scanned.

**What does "2 missing" mean?** These files were not there in the last scan. If you moved them, the note is gone after the new place has been scanned. The **Missing files** filter shows all affected models.
**Where is my data?** In the data folder next to modelkeeper.exe: catalog, settings, thumbnails, backups and a log (modelkeeper.log). **Open data folder** in the settings shows it.
**An archive is marked as broken.** The checksum of a file inside it does not match. Best download it again; modelkeeper does not touch the file itself.

slicer.title: Slicer
slicer.systemDefault: the program Windows uses for the file type
slicer.hint: "Open in slicer" always gives the slicer a read-only copy (in the modelkeeper folder under data\open), never the original file. So the slicer cannot overwrite anything in your collection. Copies are removed after 7 days; what you save next to them yourself stays.
slicer.openHint: Opens a read-only copy in the slicer. The original stays untouched.
slicer.opened: {{name}} was opened in the slicer as a copy. Save slicer projects somewhere of your own.

nav.label: Navigation
nav.waitingHint: Models from an import whose files were not found yet. A scan that finds them links them up.

catalogMode.hint: Cataloging: pick a model, type tags and press Enter. As soon as a model has tags, it leaves this list and the next one is up. ← and → move on without tagging.
catalogMode.detailHint: Enter adds the tags, then the next model follows.

empty.noFolders: Add your model folders under "Folders", local or on the NAS, and start a scan.
empty.notScanned: Start a scan under "Folders". Models appear once the scan of a folder has finished – for the first scan of a large collection on the NAS, that can take a while.
empty.cataloged: Every model has at least one tag.
empty.waitingTitle: No model is waiting for its files.

dataDir.downloads: The modelkeeper folder is in Downloads ({{path}}). Downloads is often cleaned up – move the whole modelkeeper folder to a permanent place (e.g. Documents) while the app is closed.
dataDir.synced: The modelkeeper folder is in a synced folder ({{path}}, e.g. OneDrive or Dropbox). Sync tools can damage the catalog while modelkeeper runs. Move the modelkeeper folder elsewhere and use Settings → Second backup folder for the cloud copy instead.

export.title: Export and import
export.intro: One file with everything you entered: tags, notes, favorites, print status, edited names and creators, corrections of the detection, the thumbnails you chose, your folders and detection settings. It is enough to restore your work into an empty catalog – on this PC or another one – even without the backups.
export.done: Exported {{models}} models, {{tags}} tags, {{overrides}} corrections and {{thumbnails}} thumbnails to {{path}}.
export.hint: Every backup also contains such a file (catalog-export.json), and so does every copy in the second backup folder. The file is plain JSON, readable with any text editor.
export.failed: The export could not be written to {{path}}.

import.title: Import cataloging work
import.contains: The file contains {{models}} models, {{tags}} tags, {{overrides}} corrections and {{thumbnails}} thumbnails.
import.rootsHint: Where are these folders on this PC? Choose the matching folder of this catalog, add it as a new folder, or skip it.
import.skipRoot: Skip (models are found by their files later)
import.relocateHint: If the files are at a new place now (new NAS, other drive letter), choose the folder at its new path – or add it as a new folder.
import.byContent: {{n}} found by their files (moved or renamed)
import.new: {{n}} not found yet – kept with their data and linked up when a scan finds their files
import.notesKept_one: {{n}} model has different notes here – both texts are kept.
import.notesKept_other: {{n}} models have different notes here – both texts are kept.
import.safeHint: The import only adds: nothing you entered in this catalog is removed or overwritten, and a backup is made first. You can import the same file again without harm.
import.settings: Also take over file types and detection rules
import.done: Imported: {{models}} models ({{waiting}} wait for a scan), {{tags}} tags added, {{overrides}} corrections, {{thumbnails}} thumbnails.
import.tooNew: {{path}} was exported by a newer modelkeeper. Update modelkeeper first.

history.title: Recent changes
history.intro: Tags, fields and favorites you changed. The newest change can be undone – also with Ctrl+Z anywhere outside a text field.
history.undoneSkipped_one: Undone: {{what}} – {{n}} model was changed in another way since and was left as it is.
history.undoneSkipped_other: Undone: {{what}} – {{n}} models were changed in another way since and were left as they are.
history.needsDetection: This change can only be undone together with a detection run.

tagManager.title: Tags
tagManager.intro: Rename or delete a tag for all its models at once. Renaming to an existing tag merges the two – handy for typos. Every change can be undone.
tagManager.confirmMerge:
Merge {{from}} into {{to}}?

{{to}} already has {{n}} models; afterwards all models of {{from}} carry {{to}}.
tagManager.confirmDelete_one:
Delete the tag {{name}}?

It is removed from {{n}} model. You can undo this.
tagManager.confirmDelete_other:
Delete the tag {{name}}?

It is removed from {{n}} models. You can undo this.

config.title: Configuration
config.intro: Settings and the list of folders as a JSON file – to set up another PC or a fresh installation the same way. Your cataloging work (tags, notes …) is in the export above.
config.detection: File types and detection rules ({{types}} file types, {{parts}} part names, {{sizes}} size marks)
config.program: Language ({{lang}}) and NAS rescan interval ({{hours}} h)
config.machine: Paths on that PC: slicer program and second backup folder (only taken over where they exist here)
config.rootsHint: Folders not found here can be added later, or mapped to another path with an import of the catalog export.
config.safeHint: Changed file types make a backup first and update the catalog; added folders are scanned.

moved.text: modelkeeper was moved (its data folder was at {{from}} before). Catalog, thumbnails, backups and settings came along.
moved.roots_one: This folder seems to have moved along – update its path?
moved.roots_other: These {{count}} folders seem to have moved along – update their paths?
